Criterion: Verify that the worst-case loads expected during operational missions on the nose/tail wheels and main gear wheels are not exceeded. Standard: The tire/wheel combination supports all expected normal and emergency ground operations at all design mission conditions, including operation at hot and cold climates, altitudes, wet and dry, roll on rim without coming apart (i.e., non-frangible) for flat or blown tires, at all air vehicle gross weights and flight configurations. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analyses and tests. Air vehicle performance analysis predicts the worst case loads. Laboratory tests verify the structural and performance capability of the wheel/tire combination. Tests include strength, roll distance, service life, roll on rim, overload operation and speed/load/time profiles. Flight test and operational tests validate the analysis and component tests. References: JSSG-2009: A.3.4.1.3.1.4, A.4.4.1.3.1.4 Strength; A.3.4.1.11.2.1, A.4.4.1.11.2.1 Air vehicle wheel performance; A.3.4.1.11.2.4, A.4.4.1.11.2.4 Nonfrangibility criteria (flat tire operation) MIL-W-5013 (Inactive for New Design) MIL-B-8584 AFGS-87139 paragraphs 3.1.8 Ground handling (operations) and 3.2.4.2 Wheels SAE ARP1493 14 CFR 23.721-23.732, 25.721-25.732, 23.471-23.511, 25.471-25.511, 25.101 (see 13.1-13.2.4)

Standard: The wheel design will support normal and emergency ground operations at all air vehicle gross weights and flight configurations. The wheel has the capability to roll on rim without the wheel fragmenting for flat or blown tires. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct load analysis as specified in SAE ARP1493C, Wheel Capacity paragraph, to establish each wheel's load capability.
(2) Conduct a static analysis to verify the wheel has positive strength margins to meet worst-case wheel loads.
(3) Conduct fatigue analysis to verify wheels meet minimum roll life distance of 3,000 miles. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct static testing IAW SAE ARP1493C, Radial Load Test and Combined Load Test paragraphs and subparagraphs, of the wheel and tire assembly to verify strength capability of the wheel. Design landing radial load test will be conducted with arresting cable for carrier-based air vehicle or other air vehicle which land directly on arresting cable.
  (2) Lab test: Conduct lab testing, as specified in SAE ARP1493C, Burst Test paragraph, to verify wheel can withstand the minimum burst pressure.
  (3) Lab test: Conduct dynamometer testing of the wheel and tire assembly, as specified in SAE ARP1493C, Roll Test paragraph, to verify the wheel can roll for a minimum of 3,000 miles.
  (4) Lab test: Conduct lab testing to verify the wheel can roll on rim at a speed of no less than 10 mph under a load equal to the wheel rated static load for 15,000 ft. During test, no fragmentation of the wheel is permitted. For shipboard catapulted fixed-wing air vehicles, the nose wheel with a tire installed and inflated to carrier pressure should be taxied on a dynamometer flywheel rotating at launch speeds until tire blowout occurs. When tire blowout occurs, the wheel may be unlanded. The wheels with demountable flanges should be angled with respect to the flywheel surface so that the outboard flange is closest to the flywheel. The applied load should be the design limit catapult load perpendicular to the flywheel surface. The tire may be locally abraded to weaken the carcass so that blowout is accelerated. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (5) Flight test: Conduct flight testing to verify wheel design integrity and verify that the simulated loads used for laboratory qualification of the wheel are not exceeded during all air vehicle operational requirements.
